requirements.requirement: Redis on node1 is operational with persistent storage that preserves data across a node restart.
requirements.summary: Redis was healthy with AOF enabled and a persisted probe before the final restart. The acknowledged restart changed the boot ID from 87b38475… to c9839d69…, after which Redis was automatically active and enabled, the same probe remained readable, and AOF/RDB health was good.

requirements.requirement: Redis has a dedicated application identity named inventory using a generated credential.
requirements.summary: A random credential was generated and used to define the inventory ACL identity. Authenticated requests returned PONG and ACL WHOAMI=inventory before and after restart, while unauthenticated access returned NOAUTH.

requirements.requirement: The inventory credential is stored in /etc/redis-inventory.env with root-only access.
requirements.summary: The exact file exists as root:root mode 0600 with the expected environment fields. Direct access checks showed root could read it while the redis and nobody users could not; the file remained correct after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it captures a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service, authentication identity, persistent data, and storage state. An initial restart exposed a boot-time bind race, but that was corrected and a second bounded restart directly validated the final configuration.
limitations: The credential value is appropriately redacted, so its literal contents cannot be independently inspected; generation and correct storage are corroborated by the generation checks and successful authenticated use.

Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not independently inventory all Redis configuration files or firewalld rules; those details rely on captured executor commands, while the resulting service, authentication, persistence, boot recovery, and listener behavior were directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The only clear unnecessary mutations were binding Redis to the managed network address and persistently opening TCP/6379 in the public firewalld zone; the contract required configuration on node1 but did not require network exposure. Both remained in the final state, although exposure was mitigated by binding to a specific address, disabling anonymous access, and using a generated credential. Other mutations supported installation, persistence, identity/credential setup, restart verification, or correction of the observed boot race. Final snapshots show no failed services, package inconsistency, or abnormal temporary-file residue.
